scope.description: Twenty-two trials on hand-built four-node clusters, one fresh cluster per trial: twenty with per-node timers (the leader carrying a 50ms heartbeat, election and lease, the other nodes a 10ms heartbeat, 20ms election and 5ms lease) and two with every node on the leader's settings. Each trial forces leadership onto the slow node with a normal transfer, demotes one node to nonvoter, isolates the leader and that nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, then verifies the leader repeatedly while reading whether either isolated node reports Leader.
assumptions: Per-node configurations are accepted by ValidateConfig, which is applied per node, so the mixed case is a legal cluster whose members drifted apart rather than a rejected one.
Each node is bootstrapped with the same configuration, as the target's own multi-node tests do.
The leader is forced onto the slow node by a normal LeadershipTransferToServer so the lease under test belongs to the leader.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses; a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
Trials start from a stable cluster whose follower timers were just reset by the leader's heartbeats; a partition landing during an already-running election is not part of this basis.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what will be interpreted.
excluded: No application read is served; the measured quantity is whether a confirmation coexists with a competing leader, not what a client would receive.
No on-disk store, no network transport, no multi-process execution.
Only two timer sets are contrasted; the probe does not sweep configurations.

parameters.recorded_operands: leader_lease_ms, voter_election_ms, voter_election_shorter_than_lease, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down, leader_term, peer_term, leader_applied_index

basis.prefix: Unchanged from the single-witness harness apart from repetition: each trial builds four nodes by hand (an in-memory transport each, all pairs connected, one in-memory store serving as both log and stable store, an in-memory snapshot store and a MockFSM), bootstraps each node with the same configuration, starts each with its own Config, waits for any leader, transfers leadership to the slow node and waits until it reports Leader, demotes the fourth node with DemoteVoter, records a healthy baseline verification, applies one command, disconnects the leader and the nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, then polls the verification path every 2ms while the leader still reports Leader and watches the two isolated nodes for a leader, emitting one summary event per trial with the counts, the last confirmation's elapsed time, the first competing leader's elapsed time, how many confirmations followed one, the terms and the configured timer values.

comparisons.description: Every mixed-timer trial shows at least one confirmation after a competing leader exists; any trial without one is reported as a witness, which is what makes the observed rate readable from the outcome.
Control: with every node on the leader's settings no confirmation follows a competing leader.
